answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, slashable stake before its votes or reputation count. A pulse of repeated endorsements from fresh accounts then carries little weight: influence accrues only after the accounts perform useful work over time, while provable fraud burns the stake. Splitting one identity into many does not multiply locked capital, and coordinating them ties up more funds and risks larger losses. The jetty is the entry point, not a loophole; quartz-like credentials alone confer no influence. This raises the attacker’s cost to capital, time, and exposure.
